> Identity, auth, rate-limit and world-catalog helpers for the gateway services, and `authkit-refresh-token`, which mints a simulated player's AuthKit access token (ADR-0124 D-7).

## How it answers

- **A refused mint exits 1, prints one "authkit-refresh-token:" line on stderr and no token, never echoes the refresh token, and leaves the runtime file as it was.**

Install i”
  - [A User Management issuer seed is never sent](scenarios.md#a-user-management-issuer-seed-is-never-sent): “authkit-refresh-token: no machine-user seed or runtime record for 'sim1' (looked at ~/.config/spellkave/sim-players/sim1.json and ~/.config/spellkave/player-mcp/machine-user-sim1.seed.json). Install i”
  - [AuthKit refuses the grant, and its code is named](scenarios.md#authkit-refuses-the-grant-and-its-code-is-named): “authkit-refresh-token: AuthKit refresh grant failed: HTTP 400 invalid_grant”
  - [A token from another issuer is refused](scenarios.md#a-token-from-another-issuer-is-refused): “authkit-refresh-token: refresh grant returned foreign iss (refusing — would mint a second world identity)”

## Commands

| Command | What it does | Scenarios (count) |
|---|---|---|
| `authkit-refresh-token [player]` | Spend the player's refresh token at AuthKit, keep the rotated one in the runtime file, print the access token (stdout holds only the token, so `> file` is safe). `player` defaults to `$SPELLKAVE_SIM_NAME`, then `sim1`; `SPELLKAVE_MACHINE_SEED_FILE` and `SPELLKAVE_MACHINE_RUNTIME_FILE` replace the default paths. A missing seed is installed with `scripts/sim/install-machine-seed.sh --player <name>`. | [8](scenarios.md#no-seed-the-error-names-the-install-command) |

## Recipes

**Mint an access token for a simulated player**

- [A seeded player gets a token, and the rotated refresh token goes to the runtime file](scenarios.md#a-seeded-player-gets-a-token-and-the-rotated-refresh-token-goes-to-the-runtime-file): `authkit-refresh-token sim1` · [`authkit-refresh-token.ts`](../src/bin/authkit-refresh-token.ts), [`mintMachineAccessToken`](../src/refresh-auth.ts)
  The grant goes to the AuthKit-domain endpoint with the MCP resource, so iss, aud and sub match an interactive login. `authkit-refresh-token sim1 > token` is safe: stdout holds only the token. The rotated refresh token goes to the runtime file ~/.config/spellkave/sim-players/<player>.json (mode 0600); the seed stays as installed.
  → `<access token from AuthKit>`
- [The next run spends the rotated token, not the seed](scenarios.md#the-next-run-spends-the-rotated-token-not-the-seed): `authkit-refresh-token sim1` · [`readRecordFile`](../src/refresh-auth.ts)
  Once the runtime file exists it wins over the seed, so AuthKit's rotation chain continues.
  → `<access token from AuthKit>`
